business_problem: Knowledge Orchestrator was created to prevent catastrophic corporate knowledge loss and make tacit technical and commercial know-how usable for pricing, investment and day-to-day decision-making.
solution_summary: Knowledge Orchestrator built its enterprise knowledge platform on IBM Cloud and IBM watsonx.ai using an approach it calls pre-enhanced generation (PEG). The company started by deploying its application in a Kubernetes cluster on IBM Cloud for scalability and availability, then used watsonx.ai to run content-generation algorithms that turn raw unstructured material—such as spreadsheets and sales information—into structured natural language that becomes “ground truth” for later use. Rather than relying on classic retrieval-augmented generation alone, the platform segments knowledge into domains and continuously converts operational artifacts into reusable knowledge objects, lowering hallucination risk and inference cost. The result is a searchable, AI-assisted enterprise knowledge base that employees use daily through a common interface, while the same foundation is being extended into use cases such as sales enablement, forecasting and profitability simulation for customers.

solution_components.name: IBM Cloud
solution_components.role: Hosts the platform in a Kubernetes-based cloud architecture that supports scale and availability.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Runs the PEG content-generation algorithms that transform raw operational data into structured ground truth.

data_flow: Raw and unstructured business content is ingested into a Kubernetes-hosted IBM Cloud platform, transformed by watsonx.ai into domain-specific structured knowledge, and then served back to employees and customers through a searchable knowledge experience.
business_outcome: Knowledge Orchestrator created a living enterprise knowledge base that improved employee productivity and engagement while giving the company a commercial platform it could extend into additional analytics use cases.
